title: Honest Expected Interval Length for ATE with Large Discrete Covariate Alphabets
banked_reason: No explicit globally honest sharp upper construction is established: the selected pilot-dependent factorial statistic lacks a direct variance/MGF certificate and the heavy Gaussian/fallback score is absent.
gap_reasons: The selected logarithmic-degree pilot-dependent factorial statistic lacks a direct factorial variance/MGF certificate about the unconditional target.
The heavy Gaussian/fallback score is absent.
Therefore sharp expected radius, score-root arithmetic, frontier attainment, Gaussian-radius expansion, endpoint equivalence, and fixed-alphabet Wald-radius transfer cannot be asserted.
proof_attempt_summary: The run constructed and repaired a constant-block Catoni route for the selected factorial statistic, an all-heavy override tied to the saturated one-step estimator, and an interval-level Poissonization/de-Poissonization converse.  The direct selected-factorial tail certificate and heavy Gaussian/fallback radius could not be proved under the frozen assumptions, so the sharp global upper bound, certified implementation, and endpoint bridge remain open.  The bank retains the direct same-class lower bound, deterministic range bracket, factorial-bias results, and saturated one-step local benchmark.
tldr: The same-class testing converse is established, and the strongest unconditional honest-length result is currently the bracket \(r_{n,d,M}\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\le4M\). This round separately proves the saturated one-step expansion, ratio-consistent variance, and Gaussian limit, proves that every pilot arm-cell is heavy with probability \(1-o(1)\) on the balanced local class, and corrects the heavy-light handle to impose the exact all-heavy center/variance override. The sharp global upper bound, certified computation, heavy-light radius limit, and endpoint equivalence remain open because neither the selected-factorial radius nor the hybrid heavy Gaussian/fallback radius is defined and certified.
gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, establishes the large-alphabet point-risk obstruction for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\), not directly for the ATE, and Section 6 warns that the 401(k) bootstrap and Gaussian intervals may miss nominal coverage. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 already supplies the real-mark heavy-light approximation and point-risk infrastructure, but not a directly observable tail radius. ArmstrongKolesar2021 provides finite-sample bias-aware ATE inference after imposing smoothness or shape restrictions and normal known-variance errors; it does not cover arbitrary categorical masses under fixed overlap and the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. Catoni2012 supplies a scalar score template under its own assumptions, not a theorem for this raw conditional envelope or the selected marked-factorial statistic. Expected honest length is not determined by any of these point-risk results, and regular DML theory does not cover empty saturated cells.
fill: The accepted one-mark real-outcome Chebyshev factorial estimator supplies rare-cell approximation infrastructure; a compatibility lemma exposes its selected statistic without changing its bias guarantee; a bounded-influence exponential score, using Catoni only as a scalar algebraic template, supplies a data-only tail radius proved from the unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope; recurrence-based coefficient and factorial evaluation with outward interval arithmetic supplies a finite-precision certificate; a control-arm-zero scaling identity transfers the published \(\psi_1\) hard family to the ATE model before same-class ATE-separated testing priors supply the expected-length converse; and a Hajek-projection expansion on the separately imposed balanced local submodel connects the globally honest interval to the saturated one-step benchmark.
